body:
# Independent audit of the full-rank cube stress obstruction

Source: `candidate 15d4d14834b04881`.


full-rank critical circuit, normalized signed facet and section moment
identities, failed multiplier bound, and genuine feasible depth descent.
It is not a counterexample to (OC), nor an attained local minimum.

## 1. Lattice, rank, and exact depth

The N=d+1 columns construction has exactly d columns, each balanced and
with entries plus or minus one. Their final coordinate gives the sum of
any dependence coefficients. After subtracting that multiple of the
initial column, the indicated first-family and second-family coordinates
successively force all coefficients to zero. Thus the row rank is d,
its relation space is one-dimensional, and its all-positive relation
makes the row set a minimal positive circuit. This proof works also at
m=2, where the middle list of second-family coordinates is empty.

The barycentric computation for T is exact. If an integer point has
minimum coordinate -k, nonnegative barycentric coefficients give
-dk<=sum z_i<=1-(d+1)k. Thus k<=1; at k=1 equality forces all coordinates
to be -1. Nonnegative coordinates give only zero and the d unit vectors.
The simplex is full dimensional, zero has all barycentric coefficients
1/(d+1), and the product with the cube is a full-dimensional convex body.
Its intrinsic mixed measure is precisely the finite sum of cube volumes.

The lower depth argument is valid for ALL oblique halfspaces. The coupled
outer points have uniform cube marginals and sum to the ambient zero
vector, so their closed-halfspace incidence sum is at least one pointwise.
This gives total outer mass at least V. A nonvertical halfspace through
the central center captures exactly V/2 of its central cube; a vertical
one captures the whole central cube. Threshold movement handles every
containing halfspace. Boundary fibers in vertical caps are counted.

For the matching upper bound, the displayed integer linear forms expose
one outer vertex against all other outer vertices and the center. A finite
large tilt includes exactly one desired outer cube at a central candidate,
or isolates one outer cube at an outer candidate. The chosen coordinate
tail has at most half its own cube's volume. This proves the claimed
global maximum and the unique deepest BASE, without assuming a unique
continuous maximizing center.

## 2. Critical caps and every moment identity

With L=d+1, each cap contains its own outer fiber strictly and excludes
all the others strictly because |u_j.x|<=d. Its only effective section is
the proper central cube section. Dividing all coefficients by sqrt(d)
uses a unit continuous normal; all these sections have the same positive
area S, and both their integer and continuous first moments are zero.
The chosen rho, lambda, and group multiplier satisfy the threshold and
all cap-normal equations with the stated normalization.

There are no owner ties on the relative interiors of the cube facets in
the shared representation. Intersections of distinct cube facets have
zero facet measure. The selected cap cuts of a cube facet also have zero
facet measure, since at least one nonfixed continuous coordinate has a
nonzero coefficient. Thus the indicated cap allocations are exactly the
ordinary indicators almost everywhere, with no arbitrary coincidence
trace being chosen.

For the central facet moments, I checked the reflection identity explicitly:

    B_l(-s)=-E[Y_l 1_{A<=s}]
           =E[Y_l 1_{A>s}]=B_l(s),

using E[Y_l]=0 and the atomlessness of A. The value of s is plus or minus
one, so column balance cancels every transverse continuous first moment.
Column balance also puts half the rows in each of the two tail-probability
classes, whose probabilities sum to one. This yields exactly N/2 facet
copies and the corresponding normal-coordinate moment. The outer cap
traces yield N full facet copies, with integer sum zero. Multiplying by
lambda gives d+2 copies, exactly the objective mass and first moments.

These are the free BODY-plane equations of the fixed-P shared-fiber class
in `candidate d485228e666ca27b`: its 2d planes have nonzero continuous
normal. The vertical inequalities fixing the projection T are fixed
background constraints, not additional freely moving body-plane traces.

The multiplier sum is exactly 2(d+2)/3, which is strictly larger than
1/Gamma_d for every stated odd dimension. The d=3 gap is 26/27.

## 3. Actual deformation and its exact depth

The prescribed vertex radii have average one. Their unique affine
interpolant therefore equals one at the central integer base. The
inequalities plus or minus x_k<=r(z), together with the fixed projection T,
give actual compatible fibers with the same shared-plane count, positive
radii and unchanged central volume. No independent-fiber convexification
error is hidden here.

The exact formula (8) follows by coupling the common inner cubes of radius
r_min for the central lower bound, isolating a minimum-radius outer fiber
for the matching central upper bound, and isolating each outer cube for
its own maximum. This remains an all-oblique depth calculation.

Scope clarification: that formula is mathematically valid for the finite
union with arbitrary positive outer radii and a central unit cube. Such
arbitrary radii do not necessarily give an actual compatible family;
their average could exceed one. The deformation used in the theorem has
affine radii of average exactly one, so its actual compatibility is proved.

The deformed denominator is at least d+2 by convexity. Its central
numerator is strictly below 3/2, and its outer numerator is below 2/3
under the stated bound on s. Hence its actual maximum depth is strictly
smaller than the original value. The verifier was read and rerun: all
433 exact algebraic checks passed. The all-dimensional argument rests on
the displayed rank and reflection proofs, not on this finite check.

## 4. An exact alternative cover detects the missing minimality

The example admits a useful further certificate, consistent with the
archived requirement to consider all critical-cover choices. Replace the
integer normal ell_j in EVERY selected cap by ell_1, retaining the same
full-rank continuous circuit:

    H_j^*={ (z,x): L ell_1.z+u_j.x>=0}, 1<=j<=N.

At the original body each is still a critical cap of raw mass 3V/2. It
cuts the central cube in half, contains outer fiber p_1, and excludes all
other outer fibers. Its projected group covers {ell_1.z>=0}, hence covers
the entire central and p_1 fibers. Add the ordinary isolating groups for
the other outer fibers; all those budgets are slack at raw mass V/2.

Under the stated affine-radius motion every H_j^* has the SAME actual
mass

    V[1/2+(1-s)^d],

which strictly decreases. The strict outer inclusion/exclusion margins
persist: d(1+s)<=d+1/4<L. The slack outer groups remain far below this
budget; Bernoulli gives (1-s)^d>=1-ds>=3/4, whereas each outer half-cube
has mass below 2V/3. This supplies an explicit alternative cap cover whose
every active budget decreases on the feasible path.

Moreover this alternative cover cannot satisfy the same normalized shared-
plane moment equations. On any shared cube facet F, every active cap's
integer facet first moment is exactly |F| p_1: its central contribution
has integer coordinate zero and its sole outer contribution is p_1.
The objective integer facet first moment is zero. Thus the shared-plane
equation would require

    |F| p_1 sum_j lambda_j=0,

forcing sum_j lambda_j=0. This contradicts its required positive
normalization 1/beta. The slack groups have zero multipliers and cannot
repair the equation.

Thus one legitimate critical-cover selection has the fully balanced
moment certificate in the source, while another legitimate selection
fails it exactly. This identifies the missing universal-cover information
using the same actual geometry. It does not claim that imposing every
such certificate suffices for global minimality or for the sharp OC bound.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
